scope_note: High-value NLP, LLM, agent, RAG, reasoning, evaluation, prompt-optimization, alignment, interpretability, multilingual, and efficient-LM literature, emphasizing 2025–2026 while retaining seminal earlier work. Venue status is recorded conservatively; no claim of universal state-of-the-art is made.

status_definitions.peer-reviewed: The cited venue/proceedings/journal version was peer-reviewed; arXiv may also exist as an open version.
status_definitions.accepted-not-published: Accepted to a venue but final proceedings/pagination were not verified.
status_definitions.arr-under-review: Submitted through ACL Rolling Review and not verified as accepted.
status_definitions.preprint: Public preprint or technical report; no peer-reviewed venue is claimed.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning
papers.authors: DeepSeek-AI et al.
papers.license_access: Open arXiv version; Nature page may have access controls. Official repository and model artifacts are public; repository states MIT licensing for code/model materials, with third-party bases subject to their terms.
papers.main_contribution: Shows that large-scale RL with verifiable rewards can elicit long chain-of-thought behaviors without starting from human-written reasoning traces, and packages the resulting reasoning behavior through distillation.
limitations: Most gains are on verifiable math/code/STEM tasks
long reasoning raises inference cost
reasoning can mix languages or be hard to audit
safety, factuality, and open-ended tasks require separate treatment
papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It is the clearest frontier reference for reasoning-centric RL, distillation, and compute allocation, and a baseline against which newer reasoning agents and efficient-reasoning claims should be checked.

papers.title: 2 OLMo 2 Furious
papers.authors: Team OLMo, Pete Walsh, Luca Soldaini, Dirk Groeneveld, et al.
papers.license_access: OpenReview and arXiv are open. OLMo releases weights, data, code, recipes, logs, and checkpoints; users must follow the licenses attached to each released artifact and any third-party data.
papers.main_contribution: Provides an unusually complete open replication package for a modern LM family, including full training data, recipes, logs, and intermediate checkpoints.
limitations: Does not expose every decision behind proprietary comparators
largest released scale remains below frontier closed models
data and evaluations are still English-heavy
full replication requires substantial compute
papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It turns model-development claims into inspectable artifacts, enabling work on data curation, annealing, RLVR, scaling, and reproducibility that closed reports cannot support.

papers.title: Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
papers.authors: Nathan Lambert, Jacob Morrison, Valentina Pyatkin, Shengyi Huang, Hamish Ivison, Faeze Brahman, et al.

limitations: Built on Llama 3.1 base-model terms

synthetic-data quality and benchmark decontamination are not fully solved
recipe transfer to other bases is not guaranteed
papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It is a practical reference implementation for modern SFT→preference→verifiable-reward post-training and a useful audit trail for claims about RLVR and open alignment.

papers.title: Qwen3 Technical Report

reported benchmark results are not universal across deployments

papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It is a strong current reference for open-weight multilingual reasoning models and for studying when thinking budgets help or merely add latency.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, and Douwe Kiela

limitations: Retrieval errors propagate into generation

retrieval adds latency and system complexity
papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: Nearly every modern RAG, agentic-search, grounding, and provenance system inherits its assumptions; it remains the baseline for evaluating whether newer retrieval actually helps.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.authors: Akari Asai, Zeqiu Wu, Yizhong Wang, Avirup Sil, and Hannaneh Hajishirzi

papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It is a central bridge between classical RAG and agentic self-checking systems and provides ablations needed to separate retrieval gains from critique gains.

papers.title: Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
papers.authors: Yangzhen Wu, Zhiqing Sun, Shanda Li, Sean Welleck, and Yiming Yang

open-ended generation is largely out of scope
papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It gives senior researchers a principled way to compare larger models against cheaper models with stronger decoding, rather than treating parameter count as the only scaling axis.

papers.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling

papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It is an unusually reproducible minimal intervention for studying test-time compute and is a useful foil to opaque large-scale reasoning-model recipes.

papers.title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity

results should not be generalized into a universal claim that reasoning models cannot reason

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

papers.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering

papers.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments

sandboxed scores may not transfer to unrestricted desktops

papers.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines

framework abstractions evolve quickly

papers.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
papers.authors: Chengrun Yang, Xuezhi Wang, Yifeng Lu, Hanxiao Liu, Quoc V. Le, Denny Zhou, and Xinyun Chen

papers.title: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback

papers.why_it_matters_to_senior_researcher: It is a key conceptual step from single-prompt search to end-to-end optimization of heterogeneous LLM programs, agents, and scientific pipelines.

papers.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
